metadata.datasource: EXPERIMENTAL APPROXIMATION, not a measured Vericolor II Type L spectral profile. Characteristic curves, spectral sensitivity, minimum density and mid-scale neutral density digitized from Kodak publication E-77 (September 1980), data sheet DS-8 (page 62), for KODAK VERICOLOR II Professional Film 4108, Type L. The three CMY dye spectra and the Hanatos adaptation window are inherited from the kodak_portra_160 profile by Andrea Volpato (CC BY-SA 4.0); DS-8 does not publish separate dye spectra. Density curves were fitted to the digitized Status M characteristic curves with those dyes and Status M weights, expressed above minimum density. Reference illuminant is T (3200 K), matching the Type L balance and the DS-8 tungsten exposure. The correction surface is zero (not fitted). No matched film captures establish stock fidelity. Limitations: inherited dye spectra, digitized plot precision, inferred 380-780 nm tails, no measured grain/halation/DIR, no absolute ISO calibration. The profile alone carries the film's unfiltered daylight cast; neutral prints require print-side CMY filtration or a calibrated paper, and the Ektacolor Edge paper is not calibrated for this film. A common spectral scaling and a simple rank-1 correction did not reduce the digitized mid-scale spectral residual (RMS 0.189, max 0.373 at 530 nm); the donor dye basis is retained, so this is an effective approximation, not a measured dye separation.
